title: Lifelong Planning A*
summary:
Lifelong Planning A* (LPA*) is an incremental heuristic search algorithm based on A*. It was first described by Sven Koenig and Maxim Likhachev in 2001. LPA* is an incremental version of A* that can adapt to changes in the graph without recalculating the entire graph, by updating the g-values.

LPA* maintains two estimates of the start distance g*(n) for each node: g(n), the previously calculated g-value (start distance) as in A*, and rhs(n), a lookahead value based on the g-values of the node's predecessors. If rhs(n) equals g(n), then n is called locally consistent. If all nodes are locally consistent, then a shortest path can be determined as with A*. However, when edge costs change, local consistency needs to be re-established only for those nodes which are relevant for the route.

LPA* combines ideas from the artificial intelligence and the algorithms literature. It repeatedly finds shortest paths from a given start vertex to a given goal vertex while the edge costs of a graph change or vertices are added or deleted. Its first search is the same as that of a version of A* that breaks ties in favor of vertices with smaller g-values, but many subsequent searches are potentially faster because it reuses those parts of the previous search tree that are identical to the new one.

LPA* belongs to the class of incremental heuristic search algorithms that updates the g-values from the previous search during the current search to correct them when necessary, which can be interpreted as transforming the A* search tree from the previous search into the A* search tree for the current search. Other algorithms in this class include D* and D* Lite. Incremental heuristic search has been extensively used in robotics, where a large number of path planning systems are based on either D* or D* Lite. The formal paper by S. Koenig, M. Likhachev and D. Furcy was published in the Artificial Intelligence Journal, 155, (1-2), 93-146, 2004.
